metadata.title: MeditActive | Meditation and personal growth

metadata.organizationDescription: MeditActive combines meditation, awareness, and personal growth tools to help people build sustainable habits and achieve their goals.

origin.title: Our why...
origin.description: <paragraph>We live in a society where being productive, achieving results, and moving quickly from one commitment to another take up an increasingly important part of our daily lives. In this context, it can become difficult to stop, listen to what we are experiencing, and understand whether the direction we are following truly reflects our needs and priorities.</paragraph><paragraph>MeditActive was born from a simple belief: <emphasis>growth does not necessarily mean always doing more, but also learning to recognize what truly matters to us.</emphasis></paragraph><paragraph>Meditation can be one of the tools through which we train this ability. Mindfulness practices intentionally bring <emphasis>attention to present experience and can support processes related to attention regulation, self-awareness, and emotion regulation</emphasis>. One of the main scientific reviews on the subject identified attention control, emotion regulation, and self-awareness among the possible mechanisms through which mindfulness works <citation>(Tang, Hölzel & Posner, 2015)</citation>.</paragraph><paragraph>Clinical studies also suggest interesting results, without considering meditation a universal solution. A systematic review published in <citation>JAMA Internal Medicine</citation>, which included 47 <emphasis>randomized studies and 3,515 participants</emphasis>, found that mindfulness programs can produce <emphasis>small or moderate reductions in some dimensions of psychological stress</emphasis>, particularly anxiety and depressive symptoms (Goyal et al., 2014).</paragraph><paragraph>For us, however, meditating does not simply mean relaxing. It means learning to create space between what happens and how we decide to respond. A space where we can <emphasis>observe thoughts, emotions, and sensations</emphasis>, recognize what we need, and choose more consciously how to use our time and energy. MeditActive was created to help people build this space in their daily lives.</paragraph>

vision.title: Vision
vision.description: <paragraph>We imagine a future where taking time for ourselves is not perceived as a break from life, but as a natural part of it.</paragraph><paragraph>A future where personal well-being is measured not only by what we manage to produce or achieve, but also by our ability to listen to ourselves, understand our limits, recognize our priorities, and use our energy more consciously.</paragraph><paragraph><emphasis>MeditActive aims to contribute to this change</emphasis> by helping people develop greater awareness, balance, and confidence in their abilities, so they can face changes, difficulties, and new goals without losing touch with themselves. Mindfulness research suggests that meditation practice may involve self-regulation processes that include attention, body awareness, emotion regulation, and a different relationship with our thoughts and perception of ourselves <citation>(Hölzel et al.; Tang, Hölzel & Posner)</citation>.</paragraph><paragraph><emphasis>For MeditActive, being aware does not mean eliminating difficulties, thoughts, or negative emotions. It means learning to recognize them without being automatically guided by them.</emphasis></paragraph><paragraph>The same principle can be applied to personal goals.</paragraph><paragraph>A goal should not become a constant source of pressure, but a direction to move toward while adapting the path to circumstances, abilities, and personal rhythms.</paragraph><paragraph><emphasis>Our vision is to transform personal growth from a race toward an outcome into a journey where the way we reach the destination becomes part of the outcome itself.</emphasis></paragraph>

mission.title: Mission
mission.description: <paragraph>Our mission is to make meditation <emphasis>simple, accessible, and practical</emphasis>, helping each person gradually turn it into a practice that fits into everyday life.</paragraph><paragraph>MeditActive does not ask you to suddenly change your lifestyle. It helps you begin with small moments: a few minutes dedicated to breathing, listening to your body, observing your thoughts, or simply stopping and bringing your attention back to what you are experiencing. Consistency is more important than perfection. This is why MeditActive combines meditation exercises with tools that help you <emphasis>organize your practice, define goals, observe your progress, and gradually build new routines.</emphasis></paragraph><paragraph>This approach is also consistent with findings from behavioral change research. A meta-analysis including 141 studies and more than 16,000 participants found a positive effect of goal setting on behavioral change <citation>(Epton, Currie & Armitage, 2017)</citation>.</paragraph><paragraph>Similarly, a recent systematic review of digital habit-formation interventions identifies <emphasis>self-monitoring, goal setting, reminders, and contextual cues among the most frequently used strategies</emphasis> for supporting behavioral consistency. For this reason, MeditActive does not aim only to offer a collection of meditations. The app wants to accompany people through the process that leads from:<linebreak /><linebreak /><citation>“I would like to dedicate more time to myself”</citation><linebreak /><linebreak />to:<linebreak /><linebreak /><citation>“I have created space for myself in my daily life”.</citation></paragraph><paragraph>Through guided exercises, progressive paths, and tools for observing personal progress, MeditActive aims to encourage self-awareness, consistency, and personal growth that is not imposed from outside, but consciously built by each person.</paragraph><paragraph><emphasis>A small moment of awareness can become a practice. A practice can become a habit. Over time, a habit can help change the way we approach our journey.</emphasis></paragraph>

breathing-section-1.title: Lying-down breathing with hands on the abdomen
breathing-section-1.description: Lie down comfortably and place your hands on your abdomen. Bring your attention to the movement of your abdomen as you breathe, without forcing it: feel your hands rise as you inhale and fall as you exhale. The goal is to become aware of your breath and learn to let it flow naturally.

breathing-section-2.title: Lying-down breathing with a book on the abdomen
breathing-section-2.description: Lie down and place a light book on your abdomen. Notice how your breath makes it rise as you inhale and fall as you exhale. The slight weight provides a visual and tactile reference that helps you perceive abdominal movement more clearly and make your breathing more mindful and regular.

breathing-section-3.title: Standing breathing
breathing-section-3.description: Now bring the breathing you practised while lying down into a standing position. Keep your body relaxed, your knees soft, and your torso natural. Breathe while observing the movement of your abdomen without tensing up. The goal is to maintain calm, mindful breathing even when your body has to support itself against gravity.

feet-position-section-1.title: Breathing with the earth
feet-position-section-1.description: While standing, bring your attention to both your breath and the contact between your feet and the ground. During each breathing cycle, feel your body relax and your weight move down toward the earth. Do not try to push: allow your breathing, posture, and foot support to gradually begin working together.

feet-position-section-2.title: Feeling how your weight is distributed on the ground
feet-position-section-2.description: Bring your attention beneath your feet and notice where you feel most of your weight: your heels, forefeet, inner edges, or outer edges. Shift it slowly to explore the different sensations, then find a stable, centred position. Breathe without tension and notice how small changes in foot support affect the balance of your whole body.
